faqs.question: What is the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-temperature, high-pressure flow reactor used for novel compound synthesis, reaching 450°C and 200 bar for both homogeneous and heterogeneous chemistry.

faqs.question: Can I purchase only the Phoenix Flow Reactor, without other modules?
faqs.answer: Yes. The base system covers reactions like SNAr, Boc-removal, and alkylations on its own; modules are added when your application needs hydrogenation, gas dosing, or fleet integration.

faqs.question: Can I use the Phoenix Flow Reactor without connecting it to other devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, for base-configuration applications. Modules like H-Genie or the Gas Module extend it into hydrogenation, oxidation, and other gas-based chemistry when needed.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right heated element for my reaction?
faqs.answer: Match your chemistry type: PTFE, stainless steel, or Hastelloy loops for homogeneous reactions, or CatCarts, MidiCarts, and metal-metal sealed cartridges for heterogeneous catalyst-based reactions.

faqs.question: How do I add hydrogenation capability to the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Add the H-Genie module for up to 100 bar at 99.99% purity, or H-Genie Lite for up to 50 bar at 99.9% purity, depending on your pressure requirement.

faqs.question: What types of chemical reactions can be performed with the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis in the base configuration, with hydrogenation, oxidation, and carbonylation available through additional modules.

faqs.question: Is gas phase catalytic reaction possible on the Phoenix Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: The Gas Module and Gas Module Plus support precise dosing of 14 different gases, which supports gas-based catalytic work; confirm your specific reaction with Inkarp.

faqs.question: Can I select only the elements or modules I actually need?
faqs.answer: Yes. The modular design is built specifically for this, letting you build and customize the system around your application rather than take a fixed configuration.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Phoenix II and the Phoenix – H-Genie Platform?
faqs.answer: The Phoenix II is the standalone reactor, with hydrogen generation added separately via the H-Genie module. The Phoenix – H-Genie Platform is a combined, pre-integrated system; full comparison detail is confirmed by Inkarp.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the heated elements and modules your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your target reactions are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano Phoenix™ II Flow Reactor in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform used for?
faqs.answer: It's a combined high-temperature reactor and on-demand hydrogen generation system, used for hydrogenation and related synthetic chemistry from milligram screening to kilogram-scale production.

faqs.question: What is the maximum pressure this platform reaches for hydrogenation?
faqs.answer: Up to 100 bar, which is the ceiling set by the H-Genie hydrogen generator's own output; the Phoenix reactor hardware itself supports up to 200 bar with an alternative gas source.

faqs.question: How does this differ from the standalone Phoenix II Flow Reactor?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation is included as standard here, while the standalone Phoenix II requires adding H-Genie or H-Genie Lite separately as a module.

faqs.question: How do I scale a reaction from screening to production on this platform?
faqs.answer: Start with self-fillable cartridges at milligram scale for catalyst optimization, then move to larger CatCart or cartridge configurations as the reaction scales toward kilogram quantities, without changing platforms.

faqs.question: How do I integrate my existing HPLC pump or mass flow controller?
faqs.answer: Confirm your equipment brand: Bronkhorst mass flow controllers, Knauer or Eldex Optos HPLC pumps, and Vici selector valves are all confirmed compatible, with custom integrations available for other equipment.

faqs.question: Can this platform run multiple experiments or devices at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. THS ReAction Software supports consecutive, parallel, and failover fleet operation, built for laboratory optimization and scale-up work specifically.

faqs.question: Can parameters be changed during a running experiment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Temperature, hydrogen pressure, and flow rate all adjust on the fly, without stopping the run.

faqs.question: Is data from each run exportable?
faqs.answer: Yes. The built-in mass flow controller monitors and exports hydrogen pressure and flow data for analysis and record-keeping.

faqs.question: What chemistry does this platform support?
faqs.answer: Hydrogenation, oxidation, carbonylation, SNAr reactions, Boc-removal, Claisen rearrangement, C- and N-alkylation, supercritical reactions, and heterocycle synthesis.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your scale requirements and any third-party equipment integration needed. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano Phoenix – H-Genie® Platform Flow Reactor in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: From milligram screening to kilogram synthesis. No cylinder, at any scale.
heroParagraphs: Most hydrogenation platforms make you choose: screening-scale flexibility, or production-scale output. This one doesn't ask you to pick.

Phoenix's high-temperature reactor pairs directly with H-Genie's on-demand hydrogen generation, reaching 450°C and up to 100 bar, without a hydrogen cylinder anywhere in the lab. Self-fillable cartridges and CatCarts scale the same chemistry from milligrams up to kilograms.

Temperature, hydrogen pressure, and flow rate all adjust on the fly, mid-experiment, with every run's data exportable for analysis and record-keeping. Genuine homogeneous or heterogeneous catalyst work, on one modular platform.
